original.prompt: Consider the following statements about Bharat Taxi, launched in February 2026:
items: It was launched by the Union Minister of Cooperation.
It uses surge pricing, with drivers keeping a fixed share of each fare.
Before launch, it ran a pilot in Delhi-NCR and Gujarat.
original.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
original.explain: Statement 2 is wrong. Bharat Taxi is a zero-commission, surge-free platform where drivers receive the full fare and any surplus goes back to members. Amit Shah, Union Home and Cooperation Minister, launched it on 5 February 2026 after a two-month pilot in Delhi-NCR and Gujarat.
original.source: On Thursday, Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah launched Bharat Taxi, pitching it as a driver-owned, zero-commission ride-hailing platform.

rewritten.prompt: Consider the following statements about Bharat Taxi, launched in February 2026:
items: It was launched by the Union Minister of Cooperation.
It is a surge-free platform on which drivers receive the full fare.
Before launch, it ran a pilot in Delhi-NCR and Gujarat.
rewritten.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
rewritten.explain: All three statements are correct. Amit Shah, Union Home and Cooperation Minister, launched Bharat Taxi on 5 February 2026 after a two-month pilot in Delhi-NCR and Gujarat, as a zero-commission, surge-free platform where drivers receive the full fare. Any surplus is routed back to members, and drivers also get health insurance, accident cover and retirement savings.
rewritten.source: A zero-commission, surge-free platform where drivers receive the full fare and any surplus is routed back to members.
